glossary.plain_definition: The provenance record of how a claim was produced: which models ran, which sources were consulted, who signed off. Lives in the .audit.yaml sidecar. Not the act of evaluating a verdict.

A YAML file next to each claim recording how the claim was produced: models used, sources consulted, failure info, human sign-off, and (inside its nullable `audit:` block) the analyst-vs-auditor comparison. Despite the name, most of it is run provenance, not the audit.
confusables: auditSchema (Zod schema for the whole sidecar)

glossary.plain_definition: The fourth pipeline agent. It re-judges a claim from the same evidence without seeing the analyst's verdict, then the comparison is recorded. Docs call the role 'Evaluator'; all code (package auditor/, auditor_agent, dr step-audit, auditor_verdict) says auditor. The pipeline phase for this step is named 'evaluating'.
A single checkable statement about an entity ('PRODUCT is hosted on renewable energy'), published with a verdict, confidence level, and cited sources.
How strong the evidence behind a verdict is: high, medium, or low. A claim can be 'true' with low confidence.

A reusable question the site asks of many entities (e.g. 'excludes frontier models'). Each criterion generates one claim per applicable entity. Stored in research/templates.yaml. Unrelated to a plan's acceptance criteria.

A reusable research question (e.g. 'COMPANY publishes a sustainability report') applied across many entities to generate claims. Stored in research/templates.yaml; pipeline code calls it a 'template' (TemplateRecord, template_slug); the site and reader pages call it 'criteria'. Same object.
confusables: criteria_slug (the claim field linking back to one criterion)

glossary.plain_definition: A thing claims are about: a company, a product, or a subject.
The Evaluator's independent second opinion on the Analyst's draft verdict. Stored in the audit sidecar; disagreements go to the operator, never auto-resolved.
The pipeline agent that independently re-checks the analyst's draft verdict against the sources. Older copy and code call it the auditor.
A model that at release is top-5 on major benchmarks or larger than 100B parameters. A moving target; claim narratives state which test was applied and when.

Per-source field: 'first-party' (the entity talking about itself), 'independent', or 'unknown'. Derived mechanically from source_type (primary->first-party, secondary->independent, tertiary->unknown). Readers see first-party rendered as 'company-published' and unknown as 'unclassified'.

needs_review is a machine-set boolean in the sidecar's audit block: the auditor disagreed enough that an operator should look. human_review is the sidecar block recording that an operator actually signed off (reviewer, date, notes). `dr review` writes the latter; nothing automatic clears the former.
'Not assessed' (—) means no claim exists yet for that entity/criterion pair. 'N/A' means the pair was assessed and the criterion does not apply.
A model whose trained weights are downloadable and runnable on your own infrastructure, as opposed to a proprietary model reachable only through the vendor's service.
The human who runs dr commands, reviews drafts, and signs claims off. In v1 the same person also fills the Research Lead role (planning and queueing work).
The claim frontmatter field naming which pipeline step is in flight (researching, ingesting, analyzing, evaluating). Plans use named stages, not phase numbers.

Two meanings. On sources: a first-party publisher (source_type 'primary'). In the auditor package: the analyst's original result (primary_verdict, primary_confidence) as opposed to the auditor's (assessed_verdict). Check which axis you are on before grepping.
How often a published claim is scheduled for automated re-research (default every 60 days). Shown as the 'as of' date. Distinct from human review.
Whether a named human operator has signed off on this specific claim. Auto-published claims render as Unreviewed until a human review is recorded.
The recorded human approval of a claim, written to the audit sidecar by dr review. Distinct from PR review (code/content diff approval) and from a plan's Review history rows.
Primary (the organization's own output), Secondary (independent journalism or research), or Tertiary (advocacy, opinion, aggregators).

status is the stored claim state (draft, published, archived, blocked). Conditions like queued, under review, and stale are derived from QUEUE.md, PR state, or elapsed time; they are never written to frontmatter.

Same pipeline position, three vocabularies: the agent (noun: researcher/ingestor/analyst/auditor), the CLI step (verb: step-research/step-ingest/step-analyze/step-audit), and the claim's phase (gerund: researching/ingesting/analyzing/evaluating). Note the last column: the auditor's phase is 'evaluating', and FailureStep mixes both families ('research', 'ingest', 'analyst', 'auditor').
An entity type for things that are not a single company or product (e.g. us-data-centers, generative-ai). Not the same as a claim's topics tags.

One of eight subject-area slugs (ai-safety, environmental-impact, ...) attached to every claim and criterion. In Python code this vocabulary is the `Category` enum; on the site it is the `Category` TS type, the `topics` frontmatter field, and the /research/topics/ pages. All four are the same thing.
confusables: subject (an entity type, NOT a topic)

glossary.plain_definition: Sources were sought but none directly answers the claim either way. Not the same as an unverified entity, an unreviewed claim, or a low verification level.

The seven-value judgment on a claim (true ... false, unverified, not-applicable). In analyst code, `AnalystOutput.verdict` confusingly holds the entire VerdictAssessment (title, narrative, topics, and the verdict), not just the value.
confusables: VERDICT_ORDER (display order in TS; severity scale in Python)

glossary.plain_definition: A claim field measuring how diverse its source pool is (claimed through multiply-verified). It does not mean the claim was independently confirmed. Unrelated to an entity's verification_status (identity vetting) and to CI checks.

Unrelated despite the shared word. verification_level (on claims): how diverse the source pool is, from 'claimed' to 'multiply-verified' (shown to readers as 'Cross-verified'). verification_status (on entities): whether the entity's identity was vetted ('verified', 'unverified-startup', 'unverified-other').
The pipeline is the Python automation under pipeline/. The workflow is the whole process around it: queueing, pipeline runs, PR review, sign-off, publish, recheck.
